To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the S‐to‐R morphotype transition in M. abscesus is caused by small genetic changes that affect the production or transport of glyco‐peptido‐lipids, which are important virulence factors in the pathogenesis of this emerging human pathogen.

we identified the genetic alterations responsible for the S/R morphotype alterations of three clinically relevant M. abscesus strains and that the S/R switching back and forth is unlikely in M. abscesus.

the S/R alterations of M. absccessus are caused by different small indels or single nucleotide mutations within the non‐ ribosomal peptide synthase cluster mps1–mps2–gap or mmplb, which is involved in the synthesis or transport of glycolipid molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic basis for morphotype alterations and the development of a novel genetic tool for the analysis of the M. abscesus genome.

the identification of the genetic changes that are responsible for the characteristic morphotype alterations in M.  abscessus and provides a basis for further studies on the molecular mechanisms behind this phenomenon.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S and R variants are different species, as has been suggested previously.
the S and R morphotypes are the result of different genetic lesions within a common genetic region, which in turn leads to a loss of GPL‐biosynthesis or transport, respectively, in R morphotypes.

the S/R morphotype switch in M.  abscessus is not a result of a simple loss of a single gene, but a consequence of the accumulation of different genetic changes within the mps1‐ mps2‐gap and mmpl4b loci.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genetic alterations identified within the mps1‐gap‐mmpl4b genomic region are responsible for the loss or reduced synthesis of GPLs in R variants and that these GPLs are essential for the maintenance of the smooth colony morphotype of M. abscesus.

the S/R morphotype alterations are a consequence of the loss of a single gene in the GPL cluster and that the S/R variants are stable, genetically defined entities that are not subject to frequent switching back‐to‐forward.
the S/R alterations in M. Abscessus are caused by a limited number of genetic lesions within the GPL biosynthesis and transport cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S/R morphotype alterations of M. abscesus are caused by a loss of GPL‐biosynthesis or transport.

M. absccessus R morphotypes are characterized by a loss of GPL‐synthesis and transport, which is associated with an increased virulence in the lung of a mouse model of infection and a more pronounced persistence in the CF lung epithelial cell line CFBE‐41o, compared to S morphotypes.

the genetic lesions identified within the non‐ ribosomal peptide synthase cluster mps1mps2‐gap in M. abcessus are likely to represent the main genetic determinants for the loss of the GPL‐production or ‐transport machinery in M. a bcessus.
